explain.say: Each autumn, monarch butterflies from Canada and the eastern United States fly up to about 4,000 kilometres to a few mountain forests in central Mexico. No single butterfly makes the whole round trip.

explain.say: In spring the monarchs from Mexico fly north, lay eggs on milkweed, the only plant their caterpillars eat, and die. Their children and grandchildren carry on north, each summer generation living only a few weeks.

explain.say: The last generation of summer is different. Shorter days and cooler nights put off breeding, and it lives about eight months, long enough to fly to Mexico, wait out the winter and start back north.
These butterflies have never been to Mexico, yet they find it. They steer by the sun, using a clock in their antennae to allow for its movement, and may use Earth's magnetic field on cloudy days.

faq.q: Where do monarch butterflies spend the winter?
faq.a: Eastern monarchs spend the winter packed together on oyamel fir trees high in the mountains of central Mexico, where it is cool enough for them to rest but rarely freezes. Western monarchs winter along the California coast.
asks: Where do monarchs go in winter?
Why do monarchs go to Mexico?

faq.q: How can a butterfly that never made the trip find Mexico?
faq.a: The route is in their instincts. The autumn generation inherits a drive to fly south-west and a sun compass to keep on course, so it reaches forests its great-grandparents left.
asks: How do monarchs know the way?

faq.q: How do monarchs know which way to go?
faq.a: Monarchs use the sun as a compass. A body clock, partly in their antennae, lets them allow for the sun moving across the sky; there is evidence they also have a magnetic compass.
Monarch caterpillars eat only milkweed. They store its poisons in their bodies, which makes both caterpillars and adults taste bad to birds, and their bright orange warns predators off.
Monarchs have lost much of the milkweed they breed on and some of their winter forest, and extreme weather and pesticides harm them too. Planting milkweed and protecting the forests helps.

facts: Eastern monarchs overwinter in oyamel fir forests in the mountains of central Mexico.
Monarchs' antennae contain body clocks used by their sun compass (Merlin and colleagues, 2009).
